job.title: Sales Consultant
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a specialist assistive technology provider focused on helping people with disabilities improve mobility, independence and quality of life. They work closely with therapists, healthcare professionals and families to deliver tailored rehabilitation and equipment solutions that reduce physical barriers. Their approach combines technical expertise, client centered service and innovative products to support better long term outcomes for end users.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role involves working closely with clients, families and healthcare professionals to assess needs and deliver tailored assistive technology solutions that improve mobility and independence. The position combines technical consulting, relationship building and sales responsibility, including product demonstrations, quoting and ongoing client support. They are looking for someone empathetic, organised and commercially driven, with strong communication skills and an interest in helping people achieve better life outcomes through technology.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Consult with clients, families and therapists to assess assistive technology needs.
  • Conduct on site demonstrations and provide tailored equipment solutions.
  • Manage quoting, sales processes and follow up to ensure optimal outcomes.
  • Provide technical guidance, training and ongoing client support.
  • Maintain accurate documentation, compliance records and reporting.
  • Identify new opportunities while supporting broader sales and client engagement activities. 
SKILLS & EXPERTISE
  • Strong interpersonal skills with an empathetic approach to working with people with disabilities.
  • Technical understanding of assistive technology, biomechanics or related equipment.
  • Excellent communication and relationship building capability.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage administration and travel.
  • Commercial awareness with a proactive approach to sales and client solutions.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining compliance and professional standards.

job.title: Senior Bookkeeper contract
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT AND THE ROLE
Our client is an established privately owned business in FMCG looking for an experienced Senior Bookkeeper to take ownership of the day-to-day accounting function.

This is a broad, hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys being across the detail and ensuring the finance function is accurate, organised and running as it should. You'll work closely with senior management and have responsibility across payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash flow and general accounting.

For someone with the capability and appetite, there will also be an opportunity to get involved in reporting, analysis and improving the way financial information is used across the business. This is a full-time, permanent position working five days per week from the office.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Take ownership of the day-to-day bookkeeping and accounting function
  • Manage fortnightly payroll
  • Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable
  • Manage debtor collections and follow up outstanding accounts where required
  • Complete bank and balance sheet reconciliations
  • Monitor cash flow and maintain accurate financial records
  • Support month-end reporting and general ledger activities
  • Maintain accurate accounting records across multiple entities
  • Ensure the overall accuracy and integrity of the finance function
  • Assist with financial reporting and analysis where capability allows
  • Support improvements to finance systems and processes
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Demonstrated experience in a Senior Bookkeeper, Company Accountant or similar hands-on finance position
  • Strong bookkeeping fundamentals across payroll, AP, AR and reconciliations
  • High level of attention to detail and accuracy
  • Comfortable taking ownership of a finance function and working autonomously
  • Strong understanding of accounting processes and maintaining clean financial records
  • MYOB experience will be advantageous, although not essential
  • Strong Excel skills with an interest in reporting and analysis highly regarded
  • Experience within manufacturing, FMCG or a similar operational environment would be beneficial but isn't essential
  • Comfortable working in the office five days per week

job.title: Physiotherapist - Rockhampton
job.description:
Physiotherapist – Occupational Health & Clinical Practice | Rockhampton
  • Enjoy regular weekday hours: Monday–Friday, 8 am–4 pm, with no nights or weekends.
  • Keep your work varied: combine occupational health assessments with GP-referred physiotherapy.
  • Sponsorship available for eligible onshore candidates, with full occupational health training provided.
Are you looking for variety and a better work-life balance?
Our client is seeking a Physiotherapist to join their team in Rockhampton, Queensland, in a full-time role combining occupational health assessments with clinical physiotherapy.
Spend your mornings delivering pre-employment screening and functional assessments, then your afternoons treating patients referred by the medical centre’s GPs. It’s an opportunity to broaden your skills in occupational health while continuing to provide hands-on physiotherapy care.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Working alongside medical practitioners and clinic staff, you’ll help assess fitness for work and support patients with their treatment and rehabilitation.
Morning: Occupational health assessments
  • Conduct functional capacity assessments and review relevant medical and movement histories.
  • Undertake pre-employment screening, including spirometry, audiometry, ECGs and drug and alcohol screening, following training and within your scope of practice.
  • Maintain accurate assessment records and liaise with medical practitioners to ensure reports are complete.
  • Coordinate requests for additional medical information where required.
Afternoon: Clinical physiotherapy
  • Work closely with the medical centre’s GPs to manage physiotherapy referrals.
  • Assess and treat patients referred through WorkCover, care plans and general physiotherapy referrals.
  • Develop individualised treatment plans to support recovery, mobility and function.
  • Monitor patient progress and communicate with referring GPs to support coordinated care.
Throughout the day, you’ll maintain professional documentation, contribute to a safe clinic environment and build positive relationships with patients and colleagues.

ABOUT YOU
  • A recognised Physiotherapy qualification and current AHPRA registration.
  • Strong clinical assessment, treatment and rehabilitation skills.
  • Clear communication and the ability to build rapport with patients.
  • Good organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • A collaborative approach and an interest in developing occupational health expertise.
Previous occupational health experience isn’t essential, as full training is provided. Experience with WorkCover patients or GP-referred care would be welcomed.

WHAT'S ON OFFER?
  • Full-time, Monday–Friday, 8 am–4 pm.
  • No nights, weekends or shift work.
  • A varied caseload combining assessment work and clinical treatment.
  • Full training in occupational health screening and assessment procedures.
  • Collaboration with GPs and the wider clinic team.
  • Visa sponsorship available for eligible candidates currently in Australia.
Apply with your updated CV, or contact Vicky at vicky@hassett.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Midwife | Relocate to Coastal Melbourne | 482 Sponsorship & PR Pathway
job.description:
MIDWIVES — YOUR NEXT CHAPTER STARTS IN MELBOURNE

Build your career by the bay, with sponsorship and support to make Australia home.

Thinking about moving to Australia, but unsure how to turn the idea into a realistic plan?

Our client is seeking experienced Registered Midwives to join a welcoming public maternity service in Melbourne’s Bayside area. With visa sponsorship, relocation assistance and initial accommodation, you’ll have practical support to help you make the move and settle into your new role.

For midwives looking beyond a short overseas adventure, there is also an employer-supported pathway towards permanent residency after three years, subject to eligibility and immigration requirements.

A rewarding role, with room to grow. You’ll care for women and their babies across a maternity service supporting uncomplicated pregnancies, working alongside midwives, obstetricians and other healthcare professionals.
The team places a strong emphasis on personalised care, collaboration and helping new colleagues settle in. You’ll receive a supported orientation and access to an education team that can help you build confidence, develop your clinical skills and explore your next career step.

Eligible candidates can access:
  • Subclass 482 visa sponsorship
  • Employer support towards permanent residency after three years
  • Generous relocation assistance
  • Initial accommodation within walking distance of the hospital
  • Guidance through sponsorship, relocation and onboarding
  • Relocation support for candidates moving from elsewhere in Australia
Melbourne’s Bayside area offers coastal living with access to the city’s restaurants, shopping, arts and events. Whether you’re moving on your own or with family, it’s a location where you can build a life alongside your career.
What you’ll bring We’d love to hear from you if you:
  • Are a qualified Registered Midwife with at least 12 months of recent experience
  • Have completed a graduate program or have equivalent experience
  • Hold current, condition-free AHPRA registration, or have an application underway
  • Bring strong clinical skills, ideally across antenatal, birth suite and postnatal care
  • Value compassionate, woman-centred care
  • Communicate clearly and enjoy working as part of a team
  • Hold, or are willing to obtain, a Working with Children Check and Victorian driver licence
  • Have Australian working rights or are eligible for employer sponsorship
You must hold AHPRA registration before starting employment. To be considered, you’ll need current registration or evidence that your application is underway.

The package Alongside relocation support, our client offers:
  • Public-sector pay at Midwife Grade 2, Year 2–Year 8, according to experience, plus superannuation
  • Salary packaging and novated leasing
  • Ongoing education and career development
  • Low-cost onsite parking
  • Fitness Passport and retail discounts
  • Employee wellbeing and counselling support
Let’s talk about your move You don’t need to have every detail worked out before getting in touch. If you’re serious about taking your midwifery career to Australia, we’d be happy to discuss the role, your registration progress and the support available.

Apply now or contact Vicky at vicky@hassett.com.au for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Neonatal Intensive Care Nurse
job.description:
REGISTERED NURSE – NICU | MELBOURNE

Permanent full-time and part-time opportunities | Visa sponsorship and relocation pathways available

We’re seeking experienced Neonatal Intensive Care Registered Nurses to join our client, a leading public hospital in Melbourne,
With newly created positions following an expansion of newborn services, this is an opportunity to develop your neonatal nursing career within a modern, well-supported department.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll provide specialist care to premature and critically unwell newborns, working closely with a multidisciplinary team and supporting families throughout their babies’ treatment.
The department cares for nearly 2,000 admissions each year across 36 beds, including 18 NICU and high-dependency beds and 18 special care nursery suites.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Delivering evidence-based, family-centred neonatal care.
  • Undertaking clinical assessments, recognising deterioration and supporting critical interventions.
  • Developing and implementing individualised care plans.
  • Contributing to multidisciplinary teamwork and continuous quality improvement.
WHAT'S ON OFFER?
  • $86,819.20–$102,585.60 per year, plus allowances and superannuation, depending on experience.
  • Salary packaging benefits.
  • Permanent full-time and part-time opportunities.
  • Visa sponsorship and relocation pathways for eligible international NICU nurses.
  • Dedicated education, mentoring and preceptorship programs.
  • Support for postgraduate study and ongoing professional development.
  • Employee health and wellbeing programs.
ABOUT YOU
  • Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse, or eligibility to obtain registration for international applicants.
  • At least 12–24 months of high-acuity NICU experience.
  • A Bachelor of Nursing or equivalent qualification.
  • Strong clinical assessment skills and a commitment to safe, compassionate care.
  • A collaborative approach and a passion for supporting newborns and their families.
  • A postgraduate qualification in Neonatal Intensive Care is highly regarded.
Please contact Vicky with your updated CV and AHPRA registration number, or details of your registration status, to discuss the opportunity.

job.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is an established Australian organisation operating across a complex, project-based environment. With a significant technology and data transformation underway, the business is investing in a modern Microsoft data platform to improve how information is structured, governed and used across the organisation. This is an opportunity to join at an important stage of that journey, helping build the data and analytics capability that will support better reporting, insight and decision-making across the business.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting into the Senior Business Systems & Innovation Analyst, the Senior Analytics Engineer will play a key role in developing and maturing the organisation’s data and analytics environment.

This is primarily an Analytics Engineering role, sitting between traditional data engineering and business intelligence. You’ll work across data transformation, modelling and the semantic layer, turning data from core business systems into trusted, well-structured datasets that can be readily used for analytics and reporting.

The environment is centred around Microsoft Fabric, SQL and Power BI, so we’re looking for someone with strong analytics engineering capability who ideally also brings practical data engineering experience across areas such as ingestion, ELT, integration and modern cloud data platforms.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Develop and maintain scalable data models across the Microsoft Fabric environment
  • Build reliable transformation and ELT processes from core enterprise systems
  • Design dimensional models and reusable datasets for analytics and reporting
  • Develop and maintain semantic models supporting Power BI and self-service analytics
  • Partner with business stakeholders to translate reporting and analytical requirements into robust data solutions
  • Improve data quality, documentation, governance and development standards
  • Support CI/CD and the ongoing evolution of the organisation’s modern data platform
KEY REQUIREMENTS
  • Strong experience in an Analytics Engineer, BI Engineer or similar data-focused role
  • Advanced SQL skills and strong experience developing dimensional data models
  • Experience working with Microsoft Fabric, Azure or comparable modern cloud data platforms
  • Strong understanding of semantic modelling and Power BI
  • Practical experience with ELT/ETL, data transformation and integration
  • Broader Data Engineering experience across pipelines, Lakehouse/Warehouse architecture or data ingestion will be highly regarded
  • Strong stakeholder communication skills with the ability to connect technical data solutions to business requirements
Applications will be assessed within 5 business days and shortlisted applicants will be notified directly.

job.title: Accounting & Finance Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a well established Australian business operating within an essential services industry. Backed by a larger global group, the business is continuing to grow through acquisition and is investing in its finance capability to support the next stage of its evolution.
This newly created Accounting & Finance Manager role offers a rare opportunity to combine hands on financial management with people leadership. You'll oversee the finance function while leading the local accounts team, with the scope of the role continuing to evolve as the business grows and a new ERP system is implemented.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Reporting to the General Manager, with a dotted line into the Group Head of Finance, you'll split your time between managing the end to end finance function for an assigned business entity and leading the Accounts team across the broader operation.
Approximately half of your role will focus on preparing monthly financial reporting, managing cash flow, reconciliations and month end, while the remainder will be spent leading the Accounts team, improving processes, managing workloads and strengthening controls.
As the business continues to grow, the scope of the role will expand, providing the opportunity to take on broader responsibilities across multiple entities and play a key role in an upcoming ERP implementation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Take ownership of the end to end finance function for an assigned business entity.
  • Prepare monthly management reports, including P&L and Balance Sheet reporting.
  • Oversee month end close, reconciliations, BAS, cash flow and financial reporting.
  • Lead and support the Accounts team across accounts payable and accounts receivable.
  • Improve finance processes, controls and workflow efficiencies.
  • Partner with operational leaders to provide commercial financial support.
  • Work closely with the Group Head of Finance to ensure accurate group reporting.
  • Contribute to future acquisitions and the implementation of a new ERP system.
ABOUT YOU
  • CA or CPA qualified accountant (or close to completion).
  • Strong month end and financial reporting experience.
  • Experience managing cash flow, reconciliations and statutory obligations.
  • Previous leadership or team management experience.
  • The ability to build relationships with operational stakeholders.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and interest in developing finance processes.
  • Experience within a multi entity or operational business will be highly regarded.
WHAT'S ON OFFER?
  • Geelong location.
  • Broad leadership role combining financial management and people leadership.
  • Opportunity to work closely with an experienced group finance team.
  • Significant scope for the role to evolve as the business continues to grow.
  • Long term career progression within a growing organisation.

job.title: BI Analyst
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT
 
A leading Australian not-for-profit organisation in the community services, mental health, disability, and social care sector is seeking a Business Intelligence Analyst to join its Business Systems Transformation team.
The organisation provides services supporting individuals, families, carers, and communities, with a strong focus on recovery, inclusion, advocacy, and improved service outcomes.
 
ABOUT THE ROLE
 
As a Business Intelligence Analyst, you will support business intelligence, data analysis, reporting, and data visualisation across the organisation.
Working with the Applications & Analytics Manager, you will gather requirements, analyse data, develop reports and dashboards, and provide insights that support decision-making, continuous improvement, and external reporting requirements.
 
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Gather and document business and reporting requirements from stakeholders.
  • Collect, analyse, and interpret data to identify trends, patterns, and insights.
  • Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, and visualisations using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
  • Monitor key performance indicators and provide reporting to support organisational outcomes.
  • Maintain data integrity and resolve data quality and reporting issues.
  • Support ETL, database, and data collection processes.
  • Provide technical guidance, documentation, and training on business intelligence tools.
  • Collaborate with business and technology teams to improve data systems and processes.
  • Ensure data handling complies with relevant governance and data sovereignty requirements.
ESSENTIAL TECHNICAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business, Data Science, or related discipline.
  • Experience in business intelligence, data analysis, reporting, and business analysis.
  • Strong SQL and Microsoft SQL Server skills.
  • Strong proficiency in Power BI.
  • Experience with databases, ETL, data visualisation, and CRM systems.
  • Experience gathering and documenting business requirements.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Exposure to data warehousing or advanced analytics.
  • Experience in community services, mental health, disability, aged care, or social services is advantageous.
  • Experience with Carelink and/or MMEx is desirable.
  • Ability to satisfy relevant Australian employment screening and right-to-work requirements.

job.title: Health Assessor Occupational Health
job.description:

Are you a Registered Nurse, Physiotherapist, Exercise Physiologist or Exercise Scientist looking for a change from traditional clinical practice?
Join a growing occupational health team. Enjoy consistent weekday hours, varied assessment work and no nights, weekends or shift work.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced healthcare professional—or someone looking to move into occupational health—with full training and ongoing support provided.

WHAT’S ON OFFER?
  • Generous remuneration package
  • Monday to Friday, 8am–4pm
  • No weekends, night shifts or rotating rosters
  • Full training and ongoing support
  • Varied work across a broad range of industries
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Opportunity to develop specialist occupational health skills
THE ROLE

You will conduct pre-employment medicals and occupational health assessments for employees and candidates across a broad range of industries.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Conducting pre-employment health assessments
  • Drug and alcohol screening
  • Spirometry and audiometry
  • ECG testing
  • Functional capacity assessments
  • Completing assessments in line with client and clinical requirements
  • Reviewing documentation for accuracy and completeness
  • Following up medical information and GP correspondence where required
  • Maintaining accurate, confidential and compliant patient records

  • Flexibility to work across both Gladstone and Rockhampton
  • Previous experience in occupational health, general practice, primary healthcare or clinical assessments is advantageous but not essential
Ready for a change? If you are looking for strong earning potential, consistent weekday hours and an opportunity to build a career in occupational health, we would love to hear from you.

Apply through SEEK or contact Vicky confidentially at vicky@hassett.com.au.

job.title: Finance Team Lead
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT & THE ROLE

Our client is a rapidly growing technology business operating within the healthcare sector. Following changes across the finance leadership team, they are creating a broader Finance Team Lead position to sit directly underneath the Head of Finance and lead the financial operations and reporting function. You will lead a team of four across financial accounting, revenue, AP and AR, while working closely with an established FP&A function.

The opportunity will suit someone who likes getting into the detail, working out what isn't working and actually fixing it. You'll have significant exposure to senior leadership and the opportunity to build a finance function capable of supporting the next stage of the business's growth.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Take ownership of the day-to-day financial operations and reporting function.
  • Lead, coach and develop a team across financial accounting, revenue, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable.
  • Oversee month-end reporting, reconciliations and the integrity of financial information.
  • Review existing finance processes, identify weaknesses and implement practical improvements.
  • Strengthen controls, reporting and processes as transaction volumes increase with business growth.
  • Work closely with the Head of Finance to continue improving the capability and structure of the finance function.
  • Drive process improvement and automation rather than accepting inefficient legacy processes.
  • Maintain oversight across revenue accounting, debtors, creditors and broader financial operations.
  • Work closely with the FP&A team and wider business to ensure accurate and useful financial information.
  • Build capability and accountability across the team while remaining prepared to get into the detail yourself.
  • Work directly with senior leadership on financial and operational matters as required.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Strong technical accounting background with experience across financial reporting and financial operations.
  • Commercial/industry finance experience, ideally within a growing or changing organisation.
  • Previous experience leading, coaching or developing accounting staff.
  • Genuine examples of identifying finance problems, developing solutions and implementing the change yourself.
  • Experience improving processes, controls, reporting or systems within a finance function.
  • Exposure to finance transformation or a well-developed finance environment that has given you a clear understanding of what good looks like.
  • Comfortable remaining hands-on while taking broader ownership of a finance function.
  • Able to operate independently and make decisions without needing constant escalation.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and confidence dealing directly with senior executives.
  • Able to prioritise effectively in a fast-moving environment with significant competing demands.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is an established product based business operating across Australia and international markets. With a combination of manufacturing, supply chain and commercial operations, the organisation operates within a dynamic and increasingly complex environment.

The business is entering an important period of growth and transformation, with a focus on strengthening financial capability, improving systems and reporting, and creating greater visibility across commercial and operational performance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the CFO, the Financial Controller will take a broad leadership role across financial control, reporting, commercial finance and business improvement.
This is not a traditional business as usual Financial Controller position. The successful candidate will be responsible for strengthening the financial foundations of the organisation while partnering closely with operational and commercial stakeholders to improve business performance.

A key focus will be improving reporting quality, strengthening controls and developing greater visibility across product profitability, inventory, costing and margins. The role will also play an important part in improving finance systems and processes across an internationally operating business.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead month end close, financial reporting and general ledger integrity
  • Strengthen financial controls, reporting processes and governance frameworks
  • Develop greater visibility across product profitability, gross margins and operational performance
  • Partner with operational and commercial stakeholders to support business decision making
  • Support inventory management, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting and FP&A activities
  • Drive improvements across finance systems, processes and workflow automation
  • Support statutory reporting, audit and compliance requirements
  • Partner closely with the CFO on finance transformation and broader business improvement initiatives
SKILLS& EXPERIENCE
  • CA or CPA qualified with strong Financial Controller or Senior Finance Manager experience
  • Experience within manufacturing, FMCG, industrial, wholesale, distribution or another product based environment
  • Strong understanding of inventory, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Demonstrated FP&A and commercial finance capability
  • Strong financial reporting, controls and technical accounting experience
  • Experience improving or optimising ERP systems and finance processes
  • Comfortable working across international operations and with offshore stakeholders
  • Hands on leadership style with the willingness to get into the detail
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively across finance and non finance functions
  • Mandarin language capability will be highly regarded given the organisation's international operations, however is not essential
WHAT'S IN IF FOR YOU?
  • Broad Financial Controller role with genuine commercial and operational exposure
  • Work directly with the CFO and senior leadership team
  • Exposure to international manufacturing and supply chain operations
  • Opportunity to lead meaningful finance systems and process improvement
  • Genuine scope to influence reporting, commercial insights and business performance
  • $160,000 + Superannuation + STI + LTI

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT 

Our client is a large and established organisation operating within a complex, high-volume environment seeking an experienced Finance Business Partner to support a key commercial channel.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Commercial Manager, you will work closely with sales, marketing and category stakeholders to provide accurate analysis and practical commercial advice. The role has ownership across customer and product profitability, commercial investment, forecasting, performance reporting and decision support.

This is a hands-on business partnering position for someone who can get underneath the numbers, challenge assumptions and explain where the business can improve performance. You will need to balance commercial thinking with strong financial control and attention to detail.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Partner with sales, marketing and category stakeholders across a key commercial channel.
  • Analyse sales and profitability by customer, channel and product.
  • Provide commercial advice across pricing, promotions, customer investment and product decisions.
  • Manage and analyse commercial spend, including accruals, claims, reconciliations and material movements.
  • Support the financial assessment of new products and other commercial initiatives.
  • Own key elements of the budget and forecasting process across gross margin, marketing investment and operating expenditure.
  • Investigate monthly results and prepare clear commentary on performance, risks and opportunities.
  • Review month-end journals and balance sheet reconciliations across relevant commercial accounts.
  • Deliver accurate daily, weekly and monthly performance reporting.
  • Develop financial models and complete ad hoc analysis to support decision-making.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reporting, processes, controls and commercial outcomes.
  • Take ownership of projects and issues through to resolution.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Degree qualified in accounting, commerce, business or a related discipline.
  • CA or CPA qualification.
  • Strong finance business partnering experience within FMCG, consumer goods or another high-volume environment.
  • Experience supporting major retail customers or a similarly complex commercial channel will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing commercial investment, customer rebates, promotional spend or similar arrangements.
  • Strong understanding of customer, channel, product, price and volume mix.
  • Experience working with large data sets and tracing information across financial systems.
  • Advanced Excel and financial modelling capability.
  • Evidence of using analysis to challenge decisions and improve commercial performance.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the confidence to constructively challenge non-finance leaders.
  • Inquisitive, proactive and comfortable working through detailed issues independently.
  • Able to manage a high volume of work without accuracy slipping.

job.title: Accounts Operations Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT & THE ROLE
Our client is a growing global healthcare technology business operating across Australia, the US, UK and Asia. With continued international growth and an increasingly complex finance environment, they are looking for an experienced Accounts Operations Manager to take ownership of their transactional finance function.

Reporting to the Group Finance Manager, you will lead a team of six across Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. The role owns the full procure-to-pay and order-to-cash cycles, alongside cash management and supporting the broader finance team across reconciliations and month-end.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead and develop the AP and AR teams across multiple locations, setting clear expectations, KPIs and processes.
  • Own the end-to-end AR process including invoicing, collections, cash allocation, ageing, credit control and management of overdue accounts.
  • Own the end-to-end AP process including invoice processing, approval workflows, supplier reconciliations, payments and supplier onboarding.
  • Manage daily cash positions, bank reconciliations and short-term cash flow forecasting.
  • Ensure AP and AR sub-ledgers reconcile accurately to the General Ledger and support month-end close.
  • Establish and improve SOPs, controls, SLAs and reporting across transactional finance.
  • Identify inefficiencies across AP and AR and drive practical process improvements and automation.
  • Partner with Finance, Sales, Procurement, Operations and IT to resolve issues and improve workflows.
  • Support finance transformation, ERP enhancements, UAT and implementation of new processes and systems.
  • Provide management with visibility across ageing, DSO, DPO, cash flow and operational performance.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Strong hands-on understanding of both end-to-end Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable processes.
  • 7+ years' experience within finance operations, including at least 2–3 years managing both AP and AR functions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing transactional finance teams.
  • Able to clearly demonstrate how you have improved an AP or AR function rather than simply overseeing day-to-day processing.
  • Strong understanding of how AP and AR interact with cash management, reconciliations, month-end and the General Ledger.
  • Experience establishing KPIs, controls, procedures and accountability within an accounts team.
  • Experience within a multi-entity or multinational environment will be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to ERP implementations, automation or finance transformation projects would be advantageous.
  • Strong Excel and ERP systems capability.
  • Degree qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline.

job.title: Senior Finance Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT 

Our client is a large and established organisation operating within a complex, high-volume environment. Following recent changes across its finance function, they are creating a new Senior Finance Manager position to strengthen leadership across corporate finance and finance operations.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Financial Controller, this is a broad role spanning financial reporting, planning, control, compliance, working capital and operational finance. You will combine strategic oversight with hands-on delivery, supported by a capable team including the Finance Operations Manager, while maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and delivery.
The role will suit someone who enjoys improving how a finance function operates, developing people and bringing structure to an environment that has recently undergone significant systems and process change.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead monthly management reporting, KPI reporting and wider finance submissions.
  • Coordinate the annual budget, rolling forecasts and longer-term financial planning.
  • Oversee month-end and year-end close, including accounting reviews and issue resolution.
  • Maintain balance sheet integrity through strong reconciliations, journal controls and appropriate accounting treatments.
  • Manage statutory reporting, audit, tax compliance and internal control requirements.
  • Oversee cash flow, working capital, treasury, insurance and payment controls.
  • Provide leadership across accounts payable, accounts receivable, pricing, claims and broader finance operations.
  • Monitor operational finance performance and address service, control and resourcing issues.
  • Drive improvements across finance processes, systems, reporting, automation and data quality.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders on business cases, investment decisions and broader projects.
  • Coach and develop finance leaders while building accountability across the wider team.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
